redactionNote: Examples are redacted summaries. Owner names, addresses, statement details, and booking-level records stay private unless Sawyer approves otherwise.
demandBoundary: Current benchmark-path receipts prove measurement wiring only. They do not prove booked teardowns, closed owner demand, or a market-wide willingness to switch managers.

modules.headline: Sarasota Luxe kept more March revenue away from higher-cost booking sources.
modules.whatChanged: Seascape could point to the share of revenue already coming through direct bookings instead of treating every reservation source as equal.
modules.whyItMatters: You can see whether a manager is only filling nights or also protecting what reaches the statement.
modules.boundary: One March 2026 property example. It is not a guarantee for other homes.

modules.headline: Patrick's portfolio shows the honest middle ground: real direct bookings, still limited.
modules.supportingLabel: avoided Airbnb-like cost on one booking
modules.whatChanged: The report separated a real direct-booking win from the larger booking-source problem still left to solve.
modules.whyItMatters: You get a cleaner read on what is already working and what still needs pressure.
modules.boundary: Portfolio example only. Direct bookings were real, but they were not yet the dominant source.

modules.headline: Bradenton Pool showed why cleaning-heavy stays can make platform cost harder to spot.
modules.supportingLabel: cost driver named in the report
modules.whatChanged: Seascape flagged that Airbnb's cost applied to more than nightly rent, which made the effective cost higher than the headline average.
modules.whyItMatters: You can ask whether your current manager explains the cost drivers behind each payout instead of only reporting occupancy.
modules.boundary: One property cost example. It should not be used as a universal Airbnb fee claim.

modules.headline: The owner report explains the money, the booking source, and the next action.
modules.metricLabel: revenue, booking source, cost, next action
modules.supportingLabel: owner names and booking details withheld
modules.whatChanged: The report translates activity into plain decisions: what worked, what cost more, what needs follow-up, and what is still missing.
modules.whyItMatters: You are not left guessing whether the manager is protecting the property or just sending a month-end activity dump.
modules.boundary: Redacted communication standard. It does not prove a completed external teardown outcome.
